findings.claim: Before creating the lab database, the public test helper unconditionally executes DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS relational_design_lab. A learner-owned, unrelated database with that common fixed name is irreversibly removed; the reproduced run deleted a pre-existing marker database. This violates the lab cleanup boundary.

evidence.section: DROP DATABASE — remove a database; Description and Notes

findings.recommendation: Generate a collision-resistant per-run database name, create only that name, retain ownership/state in the test process, and drop only the database that this run successfully created. Never pre-drop a fixed name.

findings.claim: task5EnrollmentDefaults does not test the requested numeric(5,2) precision or that enrolled_at defaults to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and is non-null. A scratch schema using numeric(10,2) and a nullable fixed 2000-01-01 default passed all five public tests.

evidence.section: 8.1.2 Arbitrary Precision Numbers: precision and scale

findings.recommendation: Query numeric_precision as well as numeric_scale, inspect or behaviorally distinguish the CURRENT_TIMESTAMP default without wall-clock flakiness, and reject an explicit null if criterion 4 requires every enrollment to record a time.

findings.claim: The prerequisite says psql -d postgres proves that the tests connect the same way, but on Unix psql may use a local socket while LabDatabase always constructs a TCP jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/... URL by default. Socket authentication can pass while the lab fails TCP authentication.

evidence.section: Connecting to the Database: JDBC URL forms and host

findings.recommendation: State that the tests use TCP, require PGHOST to be a hostname/IP supported by the helper, and make the prerequisite probe use the same host, port, user and database values as the JDBC URL.

findings.claim: The only documented password mechanism is PGPASSWORD. PostgreSQL explicitly warns that this variable is not recommended because some operating systems expose process environments to other users.
findings.recommendation: Prefer a password file/PGPASSFILE-compatible flow supported by the pinned driver, or at minimum disclose the official risk and use a throwaway local lab credential. Keep platform-specific file permissions explicit.
